extracted_information: The WEB CONTENT provides a detailed explanation and code implementation for hiding processes from userland on Windows using a custom kernel driver. The technique involves manipulating internal process structures to make them invisible to system monitoring tools like Task Manager.

features.name: Driver Initialization
features.description: Loading the custom driver into the kernel, setting up device creation and symbolic links for communication between user-mode applications and the driver.

features.name: Finding Process Offsets
features.description: Dynamically identifying memory offsets for process ID (PID), process name, and the list entry that links all processes. These offsets vary by Windows version.
features.technical_details: InitializeOffsets, CalcPIDOffset (iterates through PEPROCESS memory to find PID), CalcProcessNameOffset (searches for 'System' process name to find offset), listEntryOffset = pidOffset + sizeof(HANDLE).

features.name: Navigating the Process List
features.description: Walking through the doubly linked list of all active processes maintained by Windows in memory to access each process's data structures.
features.technical_details: Starts from IoGetCurrentProcess(), traverses PLIST_ENTRY using Flink/Blink pointers. Compares process names using RtlCompareString.

features.name: Unlinking the Process
features.description: Modifying the doubly linked list to remove the target process from view. The process continues to run but is no longer visible to userland tools.
features.technical_details: Modifies 'Flink' and 'Blink' pointers of the previous and next nodes to bypass the target process. Sets target's Flink and Blink to itself (currentNode->Flink = currentNode; currentNode->Blink = currentNode;).

features.name: Handling I/O Control
features.description: Enabling user-mode applications to send commands (e.g., process name to hide) to the driver, which then executes the hiding operation.
features.technical_details: DriverDeviceControl function handles IOCTL_GET_PROCESSNAME, receives process name via SystemBuffer, calls HideProcess. Userland uses CreateFile and DeviceIoControl to communicate.
